rules.statement: Classify each financial asset on the basis of both the entity's business model for managing the asset and the asset's contractual cash flow (SPPI) characteristics.
Measure a financial asset at amortised cost only when it is held in a hold-to-collect business model and its contractual cash flows are solely payments of principal and interest (SPPI).
Measure a debt financial asset at fair value through OCI when it is held in a hold-to-collect-and-sell business model and its contractual cash flows pass the SPPI test.
Measure a financial asset at fair value through profit or loss when it fails the SPPI test or is not held in a hold-to-collect or hold-to-collect-and-sell business model.

The SPPI test is met only when contractual cash flows are solely payments of principal and interest, where interest is consideration for the time value of money and credit risk on the principal outstanding.

An entity may make an irrevocable election at initial recognition to present subsequent fair value changes of a non-held-for-trading equity investment in OCI, with no recycling to profit or loss on derecognition.
An entity may, at initial recognition, irrevocably designate a financial asset as at fair value through profit or loss when doing so eliminates or significantly reduces an accounting mismatch.
Measure financial liabilities at amortised cost unless they are held for trading, are derivatives, or are designated at fair value through profit or loss.

For a financial liability designated at fair value through profit or loss, present the fair value change attributable to the entity's own credit risk in OCI unless this creates or enlarges an accounting mismatch.
Recognise a loss allowance for expected credit losses on financial assets measured at amortised cost, debt assets at FVOCI, lease receivables, contract assets and loan commitments.
When credit risk has not increased significantly since initial recognition (Stage 1), measure the loss allowance at an amount equal to 12-month expected credit losses.
When credit risk has increased significantly since initial recognition but the asset is not yet credit-impaired (Stage 2), measure the loss allowance at lifetime expected credit losses.

For a credit-impaired financial asset (Stage 3), measure lifetime expected credit losses and calculate interest revenue by applying the effective interest rate to the amortised cost net of the loss allowance.
There is a rebuttable presumption that credit risk has increased significantly when contractual payments are more than 30 days past due.
There is a rebuttable presumption that default does not occur later than when a financial asset is 90 days past due.
Always measure the loss allowance at lifetime expected credit losses for trade receivables and contract assets without a significant financing component (simplified approach).
Measure expected credit losses as an unbiased, probability-weighted amount that reflects the time value of money and reasonable and supportable forward-looking information.

Apply hedge accounting only when there is an eligible hedging instrument and hedged item, formal designation and documentation at inception, and the relationship meets the hedge effectiveness requirements.

A hedge meets the effectiveness requirements when there is an economic relationship between hedged item and hedging instrument, credit risk does not dominate value changes, and the hedge ratio is unbiased.

For a cash flow hedge, recognise the effective portion of the hedging instrument's gain or loss in OCI (cash flow hedge reserve) and reclassify it to profit or loss when the hedged cash flows affect earnings.

For a fair value hedge, recognise the hedging instrument's gain or loss in profit or loss and adjust the carrying amount of the hedged item for the hedged-risk fair value change through profit or loss.
Classify an instrument as equity only when it includes no contractual obligation to deliver cash or another financial asset and, if settled in own equity, is not a variable-number obligation.
Classify as a financial liability any contractual obligation to deliver cash or another financial asset, or to exchange financial instruments under potentially unfavourable conditions.

Classify a puttable instrument as equity, by exception, only when it meets all the specified conditions including being the most subordinated class and entitling the holder to a pro-rata share of net assets on liquidation.
Split a compound financial instrument (e.g. a convertible bond) at issuance into separate liability and equity components, measuring the liability first and assigning the residual to equity.
Deduct an entity's own equity instruments reacquired (treasury shares) from equity, recognising no gain or loss in profit or loss on their purchase, sale, issue or cancellation.
Recognise interest, dividends, losses and gains relating to a financial liability in profit or loss, and distributions to holders of an equity instrument directly in equity.
Offset a financial asset and a financial liability and present the net amount only when there is a currently legally enforceable right to set off and an intention to settle net or simultaneously.
Disclose the measurement bases and accounting policies used for financial instruments that are relevant to understanding the financial statements.
Disclose qualitative and quantitative information about exposure to credit risk, liquidity risk and market risk arising from financial instruments, including how those risks are managed.
Disclose information that enables users to understand the effect of credit risk on the amount, timing and uncertainty of future cash flows, including loss allowance reconciliations by ECL stage.
Disclose information about rights of set-off and related arrangements (e.g. master netting agreements) for recognised financial instruments, whether or not they are offset on the balance sheet.
Measure expected credit losses on financial assets at amortized cost on a current expected credit loss (CECL) basis, recognising lifetime expected losses from initial recognition with no staging.
Measure expected credit losses on a collective (pool) basis when assets share similar risk characteristics, and on an individual basis when they do not.
Reflect reasonable and supportable forecasts in the expected credit loss estimate and revert to historical loss experience for periods beyond which such forecasts can be made.
For available-for-sale debt securities, recognise credit losses through an allowance limited to the amount by which fair value is below amortized cost, rather than under the CECL pooled model.
Record all freestanding derivative instruments at fair value on the balance sheet, with changes in fair value recognised in earnings unless the derivative qualifies for hedge accounting.

Bifurcate and separately account for an embedded derivative when its economic characteristics are not clearly and closely related to the host, the hybrid is not measured at fair value, and a standalone instrument would be a derivative.
Qualify for hedge accounting only when the hedging relationship is expected to be highly effective both at inception and on an ongoing basis, with formal designation and documentation.
Defer the effective portion of a cash flow hedge's gain or loss in OCI and reclassify it into earnings in the period the hedged forecasted transaction affects earnings.
For a fair value hedge, recognise the gain or loss on the hedging instrument and the offsetting hedged-risk change in the hedged item's carrying amount currently in earnings.

Account for each business combination by applying the acquisition method: identify the acquirer, determine the acquisition date, recognise and measure identifiable assets, liabilities and any non-controlling interest, and recognise goodwill or a bargain purchase gain.
Measure the identifiable assets acquired and liabilities assumed at their acquisition-date fair values, with limited exceptions specified in the standard.
Recognise goodwill as the excess of consideration transferred plus any non-controlling interest and previously held interest over the net identifiable assets acquired.
Recognise a gain on a bargain purchase in profit or loss on the acquisition date after reassessing the identification and measurement of the acquired net assets and consideration.
Recognise contingent consideration at its acquisition-date fair value as part of the consideration transferred for the acquiree.
Remeasure contingent consideration classified as a financial liability at fair value through profit or loss after the acquisition date; do not remeasure contingent consideration classified as equity.
Retrospectively adjust provisional amounts during the measurement period, which ends as soon as the acquirer obtains the needed information and cannot exceed one year from the acquisition date.
Measure non-controlling interest in the acquiree either at fair value (full goodwill) or at its proportionate share of the acquiree's identifiable net assets, on a transaction-by-transaction basis.

In a step (business combination achieved in stages) acquisition, remeasure the previously held equity interest at its acquisition-date fair value and recognise any resulting gain or loss in profit or loss.
Expense acquisition-related costs in the periods in which they are incurred, except for costs to issue debt or equity securities recognised under IAS 32/IFRS 9.

Apply the acquisition method to each business combination: identify the acquirer and acquisition date, recognise and measure identifiable assets, liabilities and non-controlling interests, and recognise goodwill.
Recognise goodwill as the excess of the consideration transferred plus non-controlling interest and any previously held equity interest over the net identifiable assets acquired.
Measure non-controlling interest at acquisition-date fair value; unlike IFRS 3, US GAAP does not permit the proportionate-share (partial-goodwill) alternative.
Recognise contingent consideration at acquisition-date fair value, classify it as a liability or equity, and remeasure liability-classified contingent consideration each period through earnings.

Adjust provisional amounts during the measurement period, which cannot exceed one year from the acquisition date, recognising measurement-period adjustments prospectively in the period of determination.
Do not amortise goodwill (for public business entities); test it for impairment at the reporting-unit level at least annually and upon a triggering event.
Do not amortise goodwill; test goodwill acquired in a business combination for impairment at least annually at the cash-generating-unit level (no reversal of goodwill impairment is permitted).

An investor controls an investee, and therefore must consolidate it, when it is exposed or has rights to variable returns and has the ability to affect those returns through its power over the investee.
Conclude an investor controls an investee only when all three elements are present: power over the investee, exposure to variable returns, and the ability to use power to affect those returns.
Consolidate by combining like items, eliminating intragroup balances, transactions, income and expenses in full, and applying uniform accounting policies.
Present non-controlling interests in the consolidated statement of financial position within equity, separately from the equity of the owners of the parent.
Account for changes in a parent's ownership interest that do not result in a loss of control as equity transactions, with no gain or loss recognised in profit or loss.
Classify a joint arrangement as either a joint operation (rights to assets and obligations for liabilities) or a joint venture (rights to net assets) based on its structure, terms and other facts.
A joint operator shall recognise its assets, liabilities, revenue and expenses (including its share of those held or incurred jointly) relating to its interest in the joint operation.
A joint venturer shall recognise its interest in a joint venture as an investment and account for it using the equity method in accordance with IAS 28.
Presume significant influence (and therefore associate status) when the entity holds 20% or more of the voting power of the investee, unless clearly demonstrated otherwise.
Under the equity method, initially recognise the investment at cost and subsequently adjust its carrying amount for the investor's share of post-acquisition profit or loss and OCI of the investee.

Stop recognising the share of an associate's or joint venture's losses once the investment's carrying amount (plus long-term interests) is reduced to nil, unless the investor has incurred legal or constructive obligations.
Under the voting interest model, consolidate an entity in which the reporting entity holds a controlling financial interest, generally a majority of the voting interest.
Assess whether an entity is a variable interest entity (VIE) because equity at risk is insufficient, or equity holders lack power or the obligation to absorb losses and right to receive returns.

Consolidate a VIE as primary beneficiary when the reporting entity has both the power to direct the activities most significant to the VIE and the obligation/right to absorb losses or receive benefits that could be significant.
Account for an investment giving significant influence (presumed at 20% or more of voting stock) using the equity method, consistent with IAS 28.

For a defined benefit plan, recognise the net defined benefit liability or asset on the balance sheet as the present value of the obligation less the fair value of plan assets, subject to the asset ceiling.
Use the projected unit credit method to determine the present value of the defined benefit obligation and the related current and past service cost.

Determine the discount rate for the defined benefit obligation by reference to market yields on high-quality corporate bonds (or government bonds where no deep market exists) of consistent currency and term.
Split defined benefit cost into service cost (in profit or loss), net interest on the net defined benefit liability/asset (in profit or loss), and remeasurements (in OCI).
Recognise remeasurements (actuarial gains and losses, return on plan assets excluding net interest, asset-ceiling effects) in OCI immediately and never reclassify them to profit or loss.
Recognise past service cost as an expense at the earlier of when the plan amendment/curtailment occurs and when related restructuring or termination costs are recognised.
Recognise the undiscounted amount of short-term employee benefits expected to be paid as a liability and an expense in the period the employee renders service.
Measure net periodic pension cost from components including service cost, interest cost, expected return on plan assets, and amortization of prior service cost and gains/losses.
Unlike IAS 19, US GAAP permits deferring actuarial gains and losses in AOCI and amortizing the excess over a corridor of 10% of the greater of the obligation or plan assets to net periodic cost.
Recognise the funded status of a defined benefit plan (fair value of plan assets less benefit obligation) as an asset or liability on the balance sheet.
Recognise the goods or services received in a share-based payment transaction when the goods are obtained or services are received, with a corresponding increase in equity or a liability.
For equity-settled share-based payments to employees, measure the fair value of the equity instruments at grant date and do not subsequently remeasure it.

Recognise equity-settled expense over the vesting period based on the best estimate of awards expected to vest for service and non-market vesting conditions, truing up to actual; reflect market conditions in grant-date fair value with no true-up.
For cash-settled share-based payments, recognise a liability and remeasure it at fair value at each reporting date and at settlement, with changes recognised in profit or loss.
Measure equity-classified employee share-based payment awards at the grant-date fair value of the equity instruments and recognise the cost over the requisite service period.
Unlike IFRS 2 (which requires estimating forfeitures), US GAAP permits an entity-wide policy election to either estimate forfeitures or account for them as they occur.
Classify cash-settled (liability) share-based awards as liabilities and remeasure them at fair value each reporting period through earnings until settlement.
Apply optional expedients to account for contract modifications resulting from reference rate reform (e.g. LIBOR transition) as a continuation of the existing contract rather than an extinguishment.
Apply optional expedients that allow hedging relationships affected by reference rate reform to continue without de-designation when critical terms change solely due to the reform.
Apply the temporary ASC 848 relief only to eligible contract modifications and hedging relationships entered into or evaluated on or before the deferred sunset date of 31 December 2024.

Under the IFRS IBOR reform Phase 2 amendments, account for a change in the basis for determining contractual cash flows required by interest rate benchmark reform by updating the effective interest rate, not as a derecognition or modification gain/loss.
Recognise a government grant only when there is reasonable assurance that the entity will comply with the conditions attaching to it and that the grant will be received.

Recognise government grants in profit or loss on a systematic basis over the periods in which the entity recognises as expenses the related costs the grants are intended to compensate (income approach).
Present grants related to assets either by setting up the grant as deferred income or by deducting it in arriving at the carrying amount of the related asset.
Treat the benefit of a government loan at a below-market rate of interest as a government grant, measured as the difference between the proceeds and the IFRS 9 initial fair value of the loan.
Classify property held to earn rentals or for capital appreciation (rather than for use in production/administration or sale in the ordinary course of business) as investment property.
Choose as an accounting policy either the fair value model or the cost model and apply it to all investment property.
Under the fair value model, recognise gains or losses arising from changes in the fair value of investment property in profit or loss for the period in which they arise, with no depreciation.
Under the cost model, measure investment property in accordance with IAS 16's cost model (cost less accumulated depreciation and impairment), while still disclosing fair value.
Recognise a biological asset or agricultural produce when the entity controls it as a result of past events, future economic benefits are probable, and fair value or cost can be measured reliably.
Measure a biological asset on initial recognition and at each reporting date at its fair value less costs to sell, except where fair value cannot be measured reliably.
Include a gain or loss arising on initial recognition of a biological asset at fair value less costs to sell, and from subsequent changes in that measure, in profit or loss for the period.
Measure agricultural produce harvested from biological assets at its fair value less costs to sell at the point of harvest, which becomes the cost for subsequent IAS 2 inventory accounting.
Account for bearer plants under IAS 16 (property, plant and equipment) rather than IAS 41, while still measuring the produce growing on them under IAS 41.
Reflect uncertainty over income tax treatments by assuming the tax authority has full knowledge, and use the most likely amount or expected value method depending on which better predicts resolution.
Recognise deferred tax assets in full, then reduce them by a valuation allowance to the amount more likely than not to be realised, rather than not recognising them as under IAS 12.
Measure deferred taxes using only enacted tax rates and laws; unlike IAS 12, US GAAP does not recognise substantively enacted rates.
